evidence.note: Foundation-first module plan: config, errors, store, auth, idempotency, models built before the main app/routes — genuine shared-machinery-first sequencing that isolates cross-cutting concerns as their own units.

All ~12 resources plus webhook delivery and billing worker bundled into one monolithic __init__.py write instead of separate sequenced milestones; the tricky subsystems weren't scheduled as risk-first de-risking chunks.
Verification walks resources in a sensible dependency order, but done-conditions are discovered ad hoc via testing rather than pre-attached to milestones.
Restricted-key permission scoping deferred to the very end and reworked ~5 times — a cross-cutting subsystem not isolated as an early milestone, producing the rework the dimension warns about.

reasoning: The agent clearly sequenced shared foundations (config/errors/store/auth/idempotency) before CRUD resources and verified resources in a dependency-aware order, exceeding a flat to-do list (anchor 5). But it lacks explicit per-milestone done-conditions, bundled the hardest subsystems (state machine, webhooks) into a single monolithic write rather than isolating them as risk-first milestones, and left permission scoping to the end where it caused repeated rework — falling short of the concrete, verifiable, risk-scheduled decomposition of anchor 8. This places it at a 6, just above the sensible-foundation-first level.
